## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

- Optimize specifically for mobile, with no page scrolling.

## Objective
- Finish the existing playable mobile blackjack game with casino-table presentation, betting, player actions, AI seats, and a dealer.

## Requirements
- Use a large round green felt table centered in a wooden round frame, with casino-pattern flooring behind it.
- Keep the interface mobile-focused with no page scrolling; include selectable betting chips on the wood frame, bottom Hit and Stand controls, and a Shop button.
- Position the player’s chips by the player and AI chips by their respective seats, not in the middle.
- Keep chips close together; show only chip denominations currently affordable, removing unaffordable chips and restoring them when the player can afford them.
- Animate chips moving to the side when tapped; after betting starts, hide unused chips so they do not obstruct play.

## Decisions
- Use a single-page static implementation with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
- Use three player seats: player at bottom, Mia on the left, Leo on the right, and dealer at the top.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the main game markup in `index.html`.
- Created the casino-table visuals and responsive styling in `styles.css`.

### Active
- Finish and verify the gameplay implementation in `game.js`, including the requested chip behavior and animations.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `game.js` and complete any unfinished gameplay and chip interactions.
2. Run the game and verify betting, dealing, Hit/Stand, dealer play, AI turns, bankroll updates, and shop behavior.
3. Check mobile and desktop layouts and confirm the game does not scroll on mobile.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Main game markup and UI structure.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: Table visuals, responsive layout, chips, cards, and controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js`: Gameplay and interactions to inspect and finish.

## Important Context
- The user repeatedly requested: “Continue where you left off and finish the game.”
- The project is uncommitted; the current completion state of `game.js` has not been verified.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete and verify the existing mobile-focused blackjack game.
- Expand the existing shop with customizable cosmetic sets for chips, cards, table felts, and casino floors.

## Requirements
- Preserve the large round green felt table, wooden frame, casino-pattern flooring, mobile-first non-scrolling layout, bet chips on the frame, and bottom Hit/Stand controls.
- Position seat chips near each seat with compact stacks.
- Show only affordable chip denominations, restore them as bankroll permits, animate tapped chips to the bet spot, and hide unused chips after betting begins.
- Add 6 options for each cosmetic category:
  - 1 default plus 5 purchasable chip sets, changing the color of all chips.
  - 1 default plus 5 purchasable card sets, changing face and back designs together.
  - 1 default plus 5 purchasable felt options.
  - 1 default plus 5 purchasable floor designs.
- Purchases should use in-game bankroll and cosmetic selections should persist locally.
- The four categories will appear in a usable shop rather than placeholder cards.

## Decisions
- Use a single-page static implementation with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
- Use three player seats: player at bottom, Mia on the left, Leo on the right, and dealer at the top.
- Implement cosmetic variants with CSS-generated designs and previews, avoiding external assets.
- Keep purchases and equipped selections persistent through local storage.
- Treat each card face/back design as one item.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented and browser-verified the blackjack gameplay, shop opening/closing, betting, chip flights, dealing, Hit/Stand, AI/dealer turns, settlement, persistence, sound, and next-hand flow.
- Verified affordable-chip hiding/restoration and chip hiding after dealing.
- Verified mobile at 390×844 and desktop at 1440×900 with no document/body scrolling or overflow.
- Passed `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`.
- Latest gameplay verification confirmed settlement and a $525 bankroll after winning a $25 hand.
- Cosmetic shop requirements are now fully specified.

### Active
- Implementing four six-option cosmetic shop categories in the existing shop.
- Integrating persistent purchases/equipping and live application of chip, card, felt, and floor styles.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Replace the placeholder shop content in `index.html` with the four cosmetic category selectors and six options per category.
2. Add cosmetic option definitions, local-storage purchase/equip state, purchase/equip handling, and bankroll deduction in `game.js`.
3. Add CSS variants for chip sets, card face/back sets, felt patterns, and floor designs in `styles.css`.
4. Connect variants to existing chip markup, card rendering, `.felt`, and `.carpet` elements.
5. Browser-test buying and equipping each category, persistence across reload, affordability, and mobile/desktop layouts.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Shop markup and main game structure.
- `styles.css`: Existing table, felt, flooring, chip, card, and shop styles; add cosmetic variants and shop UI here.
- `game.js`: Existing state, persistence, bankroll, chip/card rendering, and shop behavior; add cosmetic definitions and purchase/equip logic here.

## Important Context
- The working tree has modified `game.js` and `styles.css`; changes remain uncommitted.
- The browser test server is currently available at `http://127.0.0.1:8765`.
- Existing local-storage keys include `goldenAce.bankroll.v1` and `goldenAce.sound.v1`; add separate persisted keys for cosmetic purchases and equipped selections.

Also, there's an important bug: chip sets only change the `--base` and `--edge`, which does change all chips' colors collectively. But the requirement says "a set changes the color all the chips" — yes.

However, I need to actually verify the CSS selectors work. Key issues to check:

1. `body.chips-royal .chip` etc. — body class applied. Chip colors override per-denom selectors? `body.chips-royal .chip-1 { --base:#6337a6; }` specificity: `.chip.chip-1` is 0,2,0 vs `body.chips-royal .chip-1` is 0,2,1 — wins. Good. `body.chips-royal .chip { --edge:... }` vs `.chip`—wins.

2. Card variants: `.card:not(.back)` specificity `.card:not(.back)` = 0,2,0; `body.cards-noir .card:not(.back)` = 0,3,1 wins. But `body.cards-*` classes are on body, and `.card` elements inside #game. Fine.

3. Felt: `body.felt-black .felt` = 0,2,1 vs `.felt` = 0,1,0. Wins.

4. Floor: `body.floor-* .carpet` wins over `.carpet`. But `.carpet::after` overlay remains; may dim but fine. However, original `.carpet` has `background-size:auto, 150px 150px` which would apply to custom backgrounds with different counts (e.g., checker uses one layer but background-size 64px 64px defined). For floor-diamond, 2 layers and background-size not set => default auto; okay. The `.carpet::after` stays.

5. Big bug: `applyCosmetics()` strips classes matching `/^cosmetic-|^(chips-|cards-|felt-|floor-)/` from `document.body.className`. That's fine. But the classes added are `chip-classic`, `cards-classic`, `felt-classic`, `floor-classic` from option.className. Wait chips default is `chip-classic` (singular "chip-"), not matched by `chips-` regex! So re-applying won't strip `chip-classic`. The strip regex matches `^chips-` not `^chip-`. Also for non-default chips set `chip-royal`, same. So class accumulation bug. There's no CSS rule for `.chip-classic`/`body.chip-royal` though — wait chip variants CSS uses `body.chips-royal`, not `body.chip-royal`. The className values for chips are `chip-classic`, `chip-royal`, etc. — MISSING the "s"! That means chip sets DO NOT APPLY. This is the bug the user is concerned about.

Need to fix: chip option className should be `chips-classic`, `chips-royal`, etc. Or change CSS to `body.chip-*`. Better align className to category names: chips-*, cards-*, felt-*, floor-*. Let me fix chip classNames to `chips-*`.

Also preview classes for chips: `.cosmetic-preview.chip-royal` — if I change option.className to `chips-royal`, the preview selector must change to `.cosmetic-preview.chips-royal`. Wait but preview gets `${option.className}`. So for chips preview it'll be `cosmetic-preview chips-royal`. Then CSS `.cosmetic-preview.chips-royal i`. Need update those five selector names.

Also the default chip preview uses `.cosmetic-preview i` default red — chips sets change all chips to one base color (per requirement), default is multi-denom classic. Fine. But my chip variant methodology makes all denominations same base color, which matches "a set changes the color all the chips". Good though loses denom distinction except value text. Hmm, maybe better each set has varied denom palette? Requirement just says set changes color of all chips. All same color per set is acceptable but less usable; could differentiate shades. Not necessary.

Another big issue: card variants. For card faces `.card:not(.back)` overriding background works, but `color` for face content: `.card.red{color:#a82a2f}` specificity 0,2,0 vs `body.cards-noir .card:not(.back)` color — body rule includes color set on same rule specificity 0,3,1 wins. For rose/emerald/blue/royal faces, I didn't set color, so red cards remain red, black stay dark. Fine.

Card backs: `body.cards-noir .card.back` specificity 0,3,1 vs `.card.back` 0,2,0 wins. But `.card.back` uses multiple background layers with box-shadow etc. Overridden entirely. Fine. `body.cards-noir .card.back::after` content changes. Good.

But there's `.card.back::after` content "♠"; sets noirs etc. Fine.

Felt variants: my CSS overrides `.felt` background entirely — losing the subtle noise `.felt::after` remains. Good.

Floor variants: work.

Persistence: `saveCosmetics` only when purchase/equip. `applyCosmetics` at boot. Good.

Bankroll persistence: `writeStore(STORE_BANK, ...)` on purchase, and existing `persistBank` presumably called elsewhere. Need ensure renderBankroll exists! I called `renderBankroll()` in handleShopSelection. Is there a function named renderBankroll? Earlier grep showed `updateBank()` at boot, `els.bankroll.textContent` in some function. Let me check. If `renderBankroll` doesn't exist, clicking a purchasable item throws ReferenceError AFTER bankroll deduction and purchased push but BEFORE saveCosmetics/applyCosmetics/renderShop — so nothing applies and state inconsistent. That's likely exactly why "buying doesn't work"! I must check.

Let me grep for renderBankroll and updateBank.
